newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dynamic Dow drives eurobourses, dlr dominant.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dynamic Dow drives eurobourses, dlr dominant.

text.p: Wall Street opened higher again on Thursday boosting confidence on already record-breaking European bourses and the dollar broke through the 1.72 mark level for the first time since spring 1994.
London, Paris, Frankfurt and several other European stock exchanges were aready trading firmly in record territory when New York opened for business and quickly put on about a quarter of a percent.

As the Dow moved up London's blue chip FTSE 100 index broke through 4,400 points for the first time. Frankfurt had already ended floor trading up more than 50 points after chalking up a new record trading high of 3,426.54 points, like other bourses boosted by the Dow's overnight 93-point rally.

On the currency front, the dollar continued to defy gravity, quickly shrugging off a slightly stronger-than expected German employment report and rallying again to touch a fresh 34-month peak at 1.7202 marks.

Analysts said the German data did not have a great impact as it was sufficiently close to expectations for a bullish dollar market to take in its stride. But it still served to underline weaknesses in the German economy compared to the United States.
Cause of the day's bourse bonhomie were the latest comments by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, whose utterances and nuances are meticulously analysed for clues to credit policy.

Having earlier plunged equity markets into despair with perceived warnings that stocks are overvalued and due for a fall, Greenspan on Wednesday reversed some of the damage in statements to a congressional committee.

Instead of repeating last week's comment that Wall Street's ascent "raised questions of sustainability", he said he did not believe in using monetary policy as a tool to influence share prices. This was interpreted as indicating the Fed would not hike rates simply to lasso the Wall Street bull.
The Dow powered ahead on his comments, ending 93.13 points higher at 6,946.
A head of sales and trading at a large London investment bank commented: "We've had a good run this morning but things have cooled off a bit,"
The blue chip FTSE 100 index has risen 277 points or nearly seven percent since the start of the year. It had broken through the 4,400 barrier by 1500 GMT.
Of six leading corporates to announce annual results on Thursday, the market reacted positively to four.

Rolls-Royce Plc powered ahead after revealing its full-year figures. Profit figures also boosted betting and hotels firm Ladbroke Group Plc, industrial conglomerate BTR Plc and engineering group GKN Plc.
Pharmaceutical giant Glaxo Wellcome Plc headed lower after its results announcement, however, and Royal & Sun Alliance Insurance Group Plc also lost ground after initially gaining on its results.

In Frankfurt German shares ended bourse trade up but off session highs reached on strength from overnight Wall Street gains and the firmer dollar which, at around 1.72 marks, is positive for German exports. The DAX index reached a new record high at 3,426.54 points before sliding on profit-taking after the index rose more than 200 points in last two sessions.
And in Paris, France's CAC-40 index of leading shares was also in record territory. Dealers said the bullish trend was supported by strong liquidity and favourable corporate results.
"This sharp rise is certainly due to Wall Street and the dollar but also to Mr. Greenspan who reassured markets," said one dealer.

French insurance company AG was up strongly amid renewed speculation about its future as a possible takeover target. But shares in carmaker Renault tumbled further as fallout continued from planned layoffs in Belgium and France.
A main focus on the currency markets was German unemployment. The adjusted total was in line with the 4.672 million leaked by German labour market sources on Wednesday.

Analysts said that while the mark may glean some support from the fact the rise in jobless was not as bad as some recent newspaper speculation, the unemployment trend remained gloomy in contrast with the U.S. labour market.
The U.S. February employment report is scheduled for release on Friday and analysts polled by Reuters expect a 230,000 rise in non-farm payrolls during the month.
At 1500 the dollar was trading at 1.7200 marks, well up from from Wednesday's close here at 1.7128.
Meanwhile gold was at lower levels as the market took stock after a scare caused by news that the Swiss central bank would sell reserves to set up a memorial fund.
Switzerland on Wednesday outlined a plan to use official gold reserves to create a humanitarian fund for victims of the Holocaust which would entail selling gold over a 10-year period.
Gold slid in reaction to the prospect of central bank gold reserve sales.
"If one bank uses reserves for this reason there are plenty of opportunities for central banks all over the world of doing something like this," one analyst said.
Gold fixed in London at $353.10 in the afternoon, up from the morning fix of $352.15, but still down from $354.50 on Wednesday afternoon.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7200 marks and 121.54 yen, compared with 1.7128 and 121.56 late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1500 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 41.6 points at 4,401.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 gained 36.86 to 2,703.05
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 52.61 at 3417.6
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $353.10 in the afternoon, down from its London close on Wednesday of 352.65.
